_README: REAL BENCHMARK TEMPLATE. 1) Copy this file to '2025.REAL.return1.json' (that name is gitignored — it holds your actual tax figures / PII and must never be committed). 2) In input_facts, fill each `value` from your source documents and DELETE any income row you don't have. 3) In expected_lines, copy each value from your professionally-prepared 1040 / IL-1040 at the line noted in _field_guide, and DELETE any line your return doesn't have. 4) Run: pnpm vitest run packages/compliance/test/verified-benchmark.test.ts — the harness auto-detects 2025.REAL.return1.json and asserts the kernel (on source-verified rule-data) ties dollar-for-dollar to your return. Any mismatch is reported per line. Values are whole-dollar decimal STRINGS (e.g. "60000"). Do NOT run until every value is filled.
prepared_by: REPLACE — your preparer, e.g. 'Jane Roe, EA #12345' (keep the word 'verified' here OR keep 'PLACEHOLDER' in benchmark_id, or the loader refuses an unattributed real-looking benchmark)
_filing_status_help: One of: single | mfj (married filing jointly) | mfs (married filing separately) | hoh (head of household).
_il_exemption_count_help: Number of IL personal exemptions claimed on your IL-1040 (Line 10 exemption allowance ÷ per-person amount). Typically 1 (single) or 2 (MFJ), plus dependents.

INPUTS (input_facts).income.wages: SUM of Box 1 (wages) across all your W-2s.
INPUTS (input_facts).income.interest: SUM of Box 1 (interest income) across all 1099-INTs.
INPUTS (input_facts).income.dividends.ordinary: SUM of Box 1a (total ordinary dividends) across all 1099-DIVs.
INPUTS (input_facts).income.dividends.qualified: SUM of Box 1b (qualified dividends) across all 1099-DIVs. Must be <= ordinary.
INPUTS (input_facts).income.capital_gain.net: Net long-term capital gain — Schedule D result (from 1099-B / Form 8949). Enter net gain; step-1 does not model losses/carryforwards.
INPUTS (input_facts).income.retirement: SUM of the federally-taxable amount from 1099-R (Box 2a). IL subtracts this on Sch M.
INPUTS (input_facts).income.social_security: Federally-taxable Social Security (1040 line 6b), from SSA-1099. IL subtracts this on Sch M.
INPUTS (input_facts).deduction.itemized.total: Total itemized deductions — Schedule A total. Enter only if you itemize; the kernel takes the greater of this and the standard deduction. Delete this row to use the standard deduction.
INPUTS (input_facts).payments.fed.withholding: SUM of federal tax withheld: W-2 Box 2 + any 1099 federal withholding.
INPUTS (input_facts).payments.fed.estimated: Total federal estimated payments made (Form 1040-ES). Delete if none.
INPUTS (input_facts).payments.il.withholding: SUM of IL tax withheld: W-2 Box 17 + any 1099 IL withholding (Schedule IL-WIT total).
INPUTS (input_facts).payments.il.estimated: Total IL estimated payments made (IL-1040-ES). Delete if none.

EXPECTED OUTPUTS (expected_lines).fed.deduction.applied: Form 1040, line 12 (Standard deduction OR itemized — whichever you used).
EXPECTED OUTPUTS (expected_lines).fed.tax.total: Form 1040, line 16 (Tax). Includes the qualified-dividends/capital-gains worksheet if applicable.
EXPECTED OUTPUTS (expected_lines).fed.tax_after_credits: Form 1040, line 22 (tax after credits). For step-1 (no additional taxes) this equals your total tax, line 24.
EXPECTED OUTPUTS (expected_lines).fed.refund_or_due: Positive = refund (Form 1040 line 34); negative = balance due (line 37).
EXPECTED OUTPUTS (expected_lines).il.base_income: IL-1040 base income (Federal AGI ± Schedule M additions/subtractions) — verify the exact line number on your 2025 IL-1040 (typically ~line 9).
EXPECTED OUTPUTS (expected_lines).il.net_income: IL-1040 net income (base income − exemption allowance) — typically ~line 11.
EXPECTED OUTPUTS (expected_lines).il.refund_or_due: Positive = IL overpayment/refund; negative = IL balance due.

_more_input_rows_you_may_add._help: Schedule A total (omit to use standard deduction)

_advanced_input_rows_complex_returns._README: For a return with a real Schedule D, rental, Form 4797 or K-1, replace the simple 'income.capital_gain.net' row with the raw facts below — the kernel derives Schedule D, the §1211(b) loss cap, the §469(i) rental allowance and the Form 4797 flow itself, exactly as it does for your uploaded documents. Use one <id> per lot / property / entity.

capital_gains_by_lot._help: Form 8949 proceeds (sales price) for this lot
Form 8949 cost/other basis for this lot
§1091 wash-sale loss disallowed (optional; omit if none)

capital_loss_carryover_in._help: Short-term carryover from your prior-year Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet (Sch D line 6). Enter as a positive number.
Long-term carryover from prior year (Sch D line 14). Positive number.

k1_passthrough_incl_form_4797._help: K-1 box 2 net rental real-estate income/(loss) (optional)
Form 4797 ordinary gain/(loss) reported through this K-1 — flows to Schedule 1 line 4. Negative for a loss.
1 = rental real estate with active participation (§469(i) special allowance may free up to 25k of loss, phased out over MAGI 100k-150k)

_multiple_returns_help: You can anchor more than one return: name additional files 2025.REAL.return2.json, 2025.REAL.return3.json, … (all gitignored). The harness auto-discovers and runs every one on each build.
_preparer_divergences_help: OPTIONAL. If your preparer made an error and TaxOS is deliberately more correct on a line, put TaxOS's corrected value in expected_lines for that concept and document the disagreement here, so the tie does not fail on the disputed line. Example: { 'fed.sche.k1_total': { 'preparer_value': '-25069', 'reason': 'Form 8582 MAGI was impossible; §469(i) allowance should be 0' } }.
